item.title: Uncomplicated pleasures in a complicated world: Bill Manhire and Jenny Bornholdt’s new poetry, reviewed
item.description: Two of Aotearoa’s greatest poets are launching new collections today. Books editor Claire Mabey reviews them both. They look good together. The crumpled white shirt on the cover of Jenny Bornholdt’s What to Wear extends a ghostly gesture to the folded paper on the cover of Bill Manhire’s Lyrical Ballads. item.title: Gone By Lunchtime: Notes from a shitstorm
item.description: On the pod this week: Wellington’s pipes, Waitangi, Henare and Collins bid farewell, the LNG debate and more. A catastrophic failure at the Moa Point wastewater plant in Wellington has laid bare a short-term crisis and a crisis of short-termism. Fortified by nothing but the balm of poo jokes, Ben Thomas relates the mood in the city and the measures under way in response, in a new episode of the Spinoff’s politics podcast Gone By Lunchtime. item.title: Clean drinking water is an essential need. Will the new RMA put it at risk?
item.description: A decade ago, failures led to thousands getting sick from contaminated drinking water in Hawke’s Bay. Now some fear the forthcoming replacement for the Resource Management Act is ‘loosening the safety net’. Drinking water is a fundamental requirement for good health; everyone drinks water, every single day. item.title: From Aroha to Vyra: The brand that sparked a debate on cultural appropriation
item.description: After facing backlash over its use of a Māori word, Australian activewear brand Aroha Collective has rebranded as Vyra. The controversy reveals why language, profit and accountability are never just ‘surface level’. On Tuesday evening, Australian-based activewear company Aroha Collective announced it was changing its name to Vyra. “This isn’t a rebrand. item.description: The Green MP on his path to parliament – and to a One Pint pinnacle.
